To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

eight weeks of cognitive tutoring not only improves numerical performance in children with mathematical disabilities, but also induces neuroplastic changes in brain activity that support remediation of the disorder.

(1) cognitive tutoring induces widespread neurobiological changes in children with MDL, (2) these neurobiological changes are correlated with performance gains, (3) the neurobiological changes normalize brain responses to numbers in children with MMDL, (4) the neurobiology of MMDL children after cognitive tutoring becomes similar to that of neurotypical children.

eight weeks of one-on-one cognitive tutoring not only remedied poor performance in children diagnosed with MLD, it also induced widespread changes in brain function that were correlated with performance gains, and machine learning algorithms showed that the brain activity patterns in these children were significantly discriminable from those of their neurotypical peers prior to intervention, but were indistinguishable after the intervention.

how the brain responds to effective intervention in children who have difficulty with mathematics.
understanding how children with mathematical learning disability (MLD) learn and how their brain changes as a result of learning.
the question of how the brain learns to solve mathematical problems and how we can use this information to improve the lives of children with MLD.
